record.paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
record.original_question: In string theories with higher-order corrections relevant to ekpyrotic or cyclic cosmology, does the compactified Milne mod Z2 × R3 space that models the reversal phase emerge asymptotically as a stable attractor when the higher-order terms are asymptotically subdominant and the matter content is a fluid with a general equation of state?

evidence.quote: What remains is an interesting issue (that can be fully addressed with the asymptotic methods used in [47]) as follows: Find whether the ‘compactiﬁed Milne mod Z2 × R3 space’ monitoring the reversal phase in the ekpyrotic and cyclic scenarios, also emerges asymptotically as a stable attractor in the dynamics of higher-order gravity when the matter content is a ﬂuid with a general equation of state.

4.5 Ekpyrosis and the Milne state with asymptotically subdominant higher-order terms
This project aims to examine the global asymptotic stability of the Milne state in string theories with higher-order corrections in an eﬀort to decide as to whether or not this state is a viable representative of the passage through the singularity in models with an ekpyrotic or cyclic phase.

artifact.category_tag: Higher-order gravity cosmology and asymptotic attractors
artifact.self_contained_problem: Consider a four-dimensional gravitational theory whose action contains, in addition to the Einstein–Hilbert term, higher-order curvature corrections (for instance, polynomial invariants in the Riemann tensor, Ricci tensor, and scalar curvature, or analogous α'-type stringy corrections), coupled to a perfect-fluid matter source with linear equation of state p = wρ for a general constant w. Within this class of theories, consider the spacetime obtained as the quotient of Milne space by Z_2 (the "compactified Milne mod Z_2") times flat three-dimensional Euclidean space R^3, which serves as a candidate model for the bouncing/reversal phase in ekpyrotic and cyclic cosmologies.\n\nAssume that, in an appropriate asymptotic regime approaching the would-be cosmological singularity, the higher-order curvature contributions are subdominant relative to the Einstein–Hilbert and matter terms. Using methods of asymptotic analysis of cosmological dynamical systems (e.g., Fuchsian or method-of-asymptotic-splittings techniques), determine whether the (compactified Milne mod Z_2) × R^3 geometry arises as a global asymptotic stable attractor of the resulting field equations, for all (or for which range of) equation-of-state parameters w. Establish either global asymptotic stability (with an explicit characterization of the basin of attraction and admissible w), or produce obstructions showing that no such stable attractor behavior occurs.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open project concerning the global asymptotic stability of the compactified-Milne reversal state in higher-order gravity with a general fluid. No published resolution was found in searches; related work treats only special cases or vacuum/scalar-field matter, suggesting the general-equation-of-state case remains open.
